\label{thm:hilbert_extension_ref}
    Let $\mathcal{H}_1$ and $\mathcal{H}_2$ be Hilbert spaces. Suppose that $U$ is a subset of $\mathcal{H}_1$ and that $\omega\colon \mathbb{R}_{>0}\to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ is a nonnegative concave function with the property that $\lim_{t\downarrow 0}\omega(t)=0$. If $G\colon U\to \mathcal{H}_2$ is a uniformly continuous map with modulus of continuity bounded above pointwise by $\omega$, then there exists a uniformly continuous map $\mathsf{G}\colon \mathcal{H}_1\to \mathcal{H}_2$ defined on the whole of $\mathcal{H}_1$ such that $\mathsf{G}|_{U}=G$. The modulus of continuity of the extension $\mathsf{G}$ is also bounded above by $\omega$.

If Gcolon Uto H_2 is a uniformly continuous map with modulus of continuity bounded above pointwise by omega, then there exists a uniformly continuous map Gcolon H_1to H_2 defined on the whole of H_1 such that G|_U=G. The modulus of continuity of the extension G is also bounded above by omega.
nodes.label: thm:hilbert_extension_ref

nodes.statement: It is possible to obtain a result similar to crefthm:stability in the dgeq 3 setting by applying . This theorem proves logarithmic stability with the L^2(Omega) norm in replaced by the H^1(Omega) norm whenever the conductivities are uniformly bounded in the Sobolev space W^2,p(Omega) with p>d. We make use of low-rank approximations and the extreme smoothing properties of the shifted NtD maps widetildeR_gammacoloneqq R_gamma-R_mathds1 and widetildeR_gamma_0coloneqq R_gamma_0 - R_mathds1. Write normtemp\,cdot\, for the HS(H_diamond^-1/2(partialOmega);H^1/2(partialOmega)/C) operator norm. To begin, we project onto finite-dimensional subspaces via P_J=Pi_JJ from . For any J, this leads to normtempR_gamma-R_gamma_0_L(H_diamond^-1/2;H_phantomdiamond^1/2/C)&leq normtempR_gamma-R_gamma_0\\ &=normtempwidetildeR_gamma - widetildeR_gamma_0\\ &leq normtempwidetildeR_gamma - P_JwidetildeR_gamma + normtempP_JwidetildeR_gamma - P_JwidetildeR_gamma_0 + normtempP_JwidetildeR_gamma_0 - widetildeR_gamma_0\\ &leq 2sup_gamma'inGamma'normtempwidetildeR_gamma' - P_JwidetildeR_gamma' + normtempP_JwidetildeR_gamma - P_JwidetildeR_gamma_0\,. Next, we control the truncation error represented by the first term in the last line of the preceding display. For any varrho geq 0, creflem:op_to_hs_rn (applied with K=J, r=-1/2, s=1/2, and q=-p=varrho(d-1) + 1/2) delivers the bound normtempwidetildeR_gamma - P_JwidetildeR_gammaleq C normtempwidetildeR_gamma_L(H^-(varrho+1)(d-1)- 1/2_diamond;H_phantomdiamond^varrho(d-1) + 1/2/C) J^-varrholeq C_varrho,d J^-varrho\,. The final inequality in the last display is due to creflem:ntd_unif_op (applied with s=-(varrho+1)(d-1)-1/2 and t=varrho(d-1) + 1/2). The constant C_varrho,d depends on varrho and d but does not depend on gamma. Thus, C_varrho,d J^-varrho also upper bounds the supremum. Now fix real numbers s and t. To control the second term in the error decomposition, we apply creflem:ntd_norm_equiv with K=J, r=-1/2, s=1/2, p=s, and q=t. This finite-dimensional norm equivalence result gives normtempP_JwidetildeR_gamma - P_JwidetildeR_gamma_0&leq C J^fracp(s,t)d-1normtempwidetildeR_gamma -widetildeR_gamma_0_HS(H^s_diamond;H^t/C)\,, where p(s,t)coloneqq (s+1/2)_+ + (1/2-t)_+geq 0 and amapsto a_+coloneqqmax(0,a). Finally, we balance the preceding two upper bounds with a judicious choice of truncation level J. nodes.statement: The squared HS(L^2_diamond(partialOmega)) norm of R_gamma C^r_d/2 satisfies sum_j=1^inftynormtemp[big]R_gamma C^r_d/2varphi_j^2_L^2&leq normtempR_gamma_L(H^-1_diamond;L^2)^2sum_j=1^inftynormtemp[big]C^r_d/2varphi_j^2_H^-1\\ &=normtempR_gamma_L(H^-1_diamond;L^2/C)^2sum_j=1^inftynormtemp[bigg]frac(1+lambda_j)^-r_d/2sqrt1+lambda_j sqrt1+lambda_jvarphi_j^2_H^-1\\ &=normtempR_gamma_L(H^-1_diamond;L^2/C)^2sum_j=1^infty(1+lambda_j)^-1-r_dnormtemp[big]varphi_j^(-1)^2_H^-1\,. The L(H^-1_diamond(partialOmega);L^2(partialOmega)/C) operator norm of R_gamma is finite for any dgeq 2 by creflem:ntd_unif_op. Since normtempvarphi_j^(-1)^2_H^-1=1 for all j, Weyl's law shows that the series in the last line of the preceding display is bounded above and below by sum_j=1^infty(1+j^frac2d-1)^-1-r_d. This sum is finite if and only if r_d>-1+(d-1)/2. The assertion follows.

        &=\normtemp{\mathscr{R}_{\gamma}}_{\mathscr{L}(H^{-1}_\diamond;L^2/\mathbb{C})}^2\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\normtemp[\bigg]{\frac{(1+\lambda_j)^{-r_d/2}}{\sqrt{1+\lambda_j}} \sqrt{1+\lambda_j}\varphi_j}^2_{H^{-1}}\\

nodes.name: weighted Hilbert--Schmidt spaces
nodes.statement: It is known that the HS(L^2_diamond(partialOmega)) norm of R_gamma C^r_d/2 is equal to the HS(H^r_d_diamond(partialOmega);L^2_diamond(partialOmega)) norm of R_gamma, which is a weighted Hilbert--Schmidt norm with information-theoretic relevance in Bayesian formulations of EIT. Additionally, these norms also equal the L^2_mu(L^2_diamond(partialOmega)) norm of R_gamma for any centered probability measure muinP(L^2_diamond(partialOmega)) with Mat\'ern-like covariance operator C^r_d . This viewpoint is especially relevant when the NtD map is regressed from paired data under squared loss, as is common in operator learning .
nodes.raw_latex: It is known that the $\mathrm{HS}(L^2_\diamond({\partial\Omega}))$ norm of $\mathscr{R}_{\gamma} \mathcal{C}^{r_d/2}$ is equal to the $\mathrm{HS}(H^{r_d}_\diamond({\partial\Omega});L^2_\diamond({\partial\Omega}))$ norm of $\mathscr{R}_{\gamma}$, which is a weighted Hilbert--Schmidt norm with information-theoretic relevance in Bayesian formulations of EIT~\cite{abraham2019statistical}. Additionally, these norms also equal the $L^2_\mu(L^2_\diamond({\partial\Omega}))$ norm of $\mathscr{R}_{\gamma}$ for any centered probability measure $\mu\in\mathscr{P}(L^2_\diamond({\partial\Omega}))$ with Mat\'ern-like covariance operator $\mathcal{C}^{r_d}$ \cite[Sec.~2.2.1]{de2021convergence}. This viewpoint is especially relevant when the NtD map is regressed from paired data under squared loss, as is common in operator learning \cite{kovachki2024operator,boulle2024mathematical}.

nodes.name: integral kernels of shifted NtD maps
nodes.statement: Theoretically, we could have worked with shifted NtD maps R_gamma-R_mathds1. These shifted operators belong to HS(L^2_diamond(partialOmega)) in any dimension dgeq 2 by creflem:ntd_unif_op and the proof of creflem:ntd_hs_any_dim. Although mathematically convenient, it is known that this relative continuum measurement model is not clinically relevant in practice. Indeed, having access to the background NtD map R_mathds1 is not a realistic assumption , and there is work that attempts to circumvent relative or difference EIT measurements . We emphasize that the availability of relative NtD boundary data is not assumed in our work.

In \cref{thm:extension_eit_kernel}, we could have replaced $\widetilde{\Psi}^\star$ with $\widetilde{\Psi}^\star_{\Gamma}\coloneqq \mathsf{T}_\Gamma\circ \widetilde{\Psi}^\star$ everywhere. Indeed, $\widetilde{\Psi}^\star_{\Gamma}$ extends $\Psi^\star$ because $\widetilde{\Psi}^\star_{\Gamma}(\kappa_\gamma)=\mathsf{T}_\Gamma(\Psi^\star(\kappa_\gamma))=\Psi^\star(\kappa_\gamma)$ for any $\gamma\in\mathcal{X}_d(R)\subseteq\Gamma$. The continuity bound \eqref{eqn:stability_kernel_out} also remains valid because $\mathsf{T}_\Gamma$ is Lipschitz.

However, for the purposes of the present paper, we do not need to consider clipping the extension $\widetilde{\Psi}^\star$, but remark that doing so may prove useful in other contexts. For example, the elliptic operator in \eqref{eqn:elliptic} with $\gamma\in \mathrm{Ran}(\widetilde{\Psi}^\star_{\Gamma})$ is well-defined, while it may not be with $\gamma\in \mathrm{Ran}(\widetilde{\Psi}^\star)$.

nodes.statement: Let widetildePsi^star be the extension of Psi^star from crefthm:extension_eit_kernel. Define the set sum Z_deltacoloneqq setkappa_0+eta_0kappa_0in Dom(Psi^star)\, and \, eta_0in K_deltasubseteq L^2(partialOmegatimespartialOmega)\,. The set Dom(Psi^star) from is compact in L^2(partialOmegatimespartialOmega) by crefcor:compact_set_kernel. Also, K_delta is compact because it is a closed subset of the compact set Ksubset L^2(partialOmegatimespartialOmega). It follows that the sum Z_delta is also compact in L^2(partialOmegatimespartialOmega) because it is the continuous image of the compact set Dom(Psi^star)times K_delta. Now fix varepsilon>0. We claim that there exists a generalized FNO Psi of the form such that sup_kappain Z_delta\,normtempwidetildePsi^star(kappa)-Psi(kappa)_L^2(Omega)leqvarepsilon\,. Under this claim, let gammainX_d(R) and etain K_delta be arbitrary. By the definition of Psi^star and its extension, normtempgamma - Psi(kappa_gamma + eta)_L^2(Omega)=normtempPsi^star(kappa_gamma) - Psi(kappa_gamma + eta)_L^2(Omega)=normtempwidetildePsi^star(kappa_gamma) - Psi(kappa_gamma + eta)_L^2(Omega)\,. By the triangle inequality, the uniform continuity estimate , and the claim~, normtempwidetildePsi^star(kappa_gamma) - Psi(kappa_gamma + eta)_L^2(Omega) &leq normtempwidetildePsi^star(kappa_gamma) - widetildePsi^star(kappa_gamma+eta)_L^2(Omega)\\ & +normtempwidetildePsi^star(kappa_gamma+eta) - Psi(kappa_gamma + eta)_L^2(Omega)\\ &leq C^star omega^starbigl(normtempeta_L^2(partialOmegatimespartialOmega)bigr) + sup_kappain Z_delta\,normtempwidetildePsi^star(kappa) - Psi(kappa)_L^2(Omega)\\ &leq C^staromega^star(delta) + varepsilon\,. This implies the assertion . It remains to prove the claim . Recall the global-to-local map G from and the local-to-global map L from . Write Psicoloneqq Psi_0circG for some Psi_0colon L^2(Dtimes D;R^J^2)to L^2(Omega) to be determined. By creflem:left_inv_pou, sup_kappain Z_delta\,normtempwidetildePsi^star(kappa) - Psi(kappa)_L^2(Omega)&=sup_kappain Z_delta\,normtemp(widetildePsi^starcirc L)(G kappa)-Psi_0(G kappa)_L^2(Omega)\\ &= sup_hin G(Z_delta)normtemp(widetildePsi^starcirc L)(h)-Psi_0(h)_L^2(Omega)\,. Since Z_delta is compact in L^2(partialOmegatimespartialOmega), the set G(Z_delta) is compact in L^2(Dtimes D;R^J^2) by the continuity of G. To find Psi_0 that uniformly approximates widetildePsi^starcirc L over G(Z_delta), we adapt ideas from the proof of . First, we associate to widetildePsi^starcirc L another operator Upsilon^star that is more compatible with existing FNO approximation theorems requiring matching domain dimensions . Second, we relate Upsilon^star back to widetildePsi^starcirc L by introducing a linear functional averaging layer. This allows us to bound the display . Last, we demonstrate that our approach indeed leads to an approximation of the form . subparagraph*Step 1. Since overlineOmegasubset(0,1)^d and T^dsimeq[0,1]^d_per, the linear restriction operator R colon L^2(T^d)to L^2(Omega) given by umapsto u|_Omega is well-defined and continuous with norm at most one. Let Ecolon L^2(Omega)to L^2(T^d) be the continuous linear extension operator from . It holds that RE=Id_L^2(Omega). Define Upsilon_0^starcoloneqq EcircwidetildePsi^starcirc Lcolon L^2(DtimesD;R^J^2)to L^2(T^d) so that widetildePsi^starcirc L= Rcirc Upsilon_0^star. Recall that dgeq 2. Define Upsilon^starcolon L^2(DtimesD;R^J^2)to L^2(T^2d-2) by bigl(Upsilon^star (h)bigr)(x_1,x_2,ldots, x_2d-3, x_2d-2)coloneqq bigl(Upsilon^star_0 (h)bigr)(x_1,x_2,ldots, x_d-1,x_d) for every h and x=(x_1,ldots,x_2d-2). The periodic function Upsilon^star (h) is constant in the last d-2 dimensions. Since widetildePsi^starcolon L^2(partialOmegatimespartialOmega)to L^2(Omega) is continuous by , and so are the linear maps E and L, the operator Upsilon_0^star is also continuous. Moreover, normtempUpsilon^star(h)-Upsilon^star(h')^2_L^2(T^2d-2)=normtempUpsilon^star_0(h)-Upsilon^star_0(h')^2_L^2(T^d) for all h and h'. We deduce that Upsilon^star is continuous. Using crefassump:main and the fact that (abusing notation) overlineDtimesDsubset (0,1)^2d-2, the universal approximation theorem for FNOs with periodic outputs shows that there exist a continuous linear extension operator E'colon L^2(DtimesD;R^J^2)to L^2(T^2d-2;R^J^2) and, for every varepsilon>0, an FNO Psi'colon L^2(T^2d-2;R^J^2)to L^2(T^2d-2) of the form such that sup_hinG(Z_delta)normtempUpsilon^star(h)-Psi'(E' h)_L^2(T^2d-2)leq varepsilon\,. subparagraph*Step 2. To relate the preceding periodic approximation result back to the claim and the display , define the linear operator Acolon L^2(T^2d-2)to L^2(T^d) by umapsto A ucoloneqq int_T^d-2u(\,cdot\,, x_d+1,ldots, x_2d-2)ddx_d+1cdots ddx_2d-2\,. This operator averages the last d-2 dimensions of the input function. Since [0,1]^n has Lebesgue measure one for all n, Jensen's inequality shows that the map A has operator norm one (with supremum achieved at the constant function mathds1). Observe that Upsilon_0^star=Acirc Upsilon^star\,. By defining Psi_0coloneqq RcircAcircPsi'circE', it holds that sup_hin G(Z_delta)normtemp(widetildePsi^starcirc L)(h)-Psi_0(h)_L^2(Omega)&=sup_hin G(Z_delta)normtemp(RcircAcircUpsilon^star)(h)-Psi_0(h)_L^2(Omega)\\ &leq sup_hin G(Z_delta)normtemp(AcircUpsilon^star)(h)-(AcircPsi'circE')(h)_L^2(T^d)\\ &leq sup_hin G(Z_delta)normtempUpsilon^star(h)-(Psi'circE')(h)_L^2(T^2d-2)\\ &leq varepsilon because both R and A have operator norm at most one. This delivers the display . subparagraph*Step 3. To complete the proof of the claim, we must show that our final approximation Psicoloneqq RcircAcircPsi'circE'circG is of the form with M=partialOmegatimespartialOmega, d_a=2d, d_m=2d-2, and d_in=d_out=1. By definition of Psi', asserts that there exist a number of layers T, channel dimension d_c, matrix S'inR^d_ctimes J^2 determining operator S' according to , and matrix Q'in R^1times d_c determining operator Q' according to such that Psi'=Q'circ L_Lcirc cdots circ L_1circ S'\,, where the nonlinear operators \L_ell\_ell=1^L map L^2(T^2d-2;R^d_c) into itself and are given in~ and . The preceding two displays show that we can write Psi= Q circRcirc FcircL_LcirccdotscircL_1circEcirc S in the form by taking S&coloneqq \,0\,&\,cdots\,& \,0\,& \,1\, inR^1times (2d+1)quadso that S=Id_L^2(partialOmegatimespartialOmega)\,,\\ E &coloneqq S'circE'circGinLbigl(L^2(partialOmegatimespartialOmega);L^2(T^2d-2;R^d_c)bigr)\,,\\ F&coloneqqAcirc Q'in Lbigl(L^2(T^2d-2;R^d_c); L^2(T^d)bigr)\,,\\ R&coloneqqRin Lbigl(L^2(T^d); L^2(Omega)bigr)\,,quadand \\ Q&coloneqq 1inR^1times 1 quadso that Q=Id_L^2(Omega)\,. The requirement that E be continuous holds because the global-to-local map GinL(L^2(partialOmegatimespartialOmega); L^2(DtimesD;R^J^2)), E', and S' are all continuous linear operators. Moreover, F is the composition of two continuous linear maps so it is itself continuous and linear. It may be identified, via~, with the constant kernel function kappacolon T^d-2toR^1times d_c given by xmapsto kappa(x)=Q'. Being constant, the function kappa is periodic and has a well-defined Fourier series. All together, these facts deliver the claimed form of the neural operator approximation.

nodes.statement: The number of inclusions is usually predicted correctly, ranging from one to four or more. We now comment on accuracy quantitatively. The first three columns of creffig:tile_shape represent the test set samples with the worst, median, and best Dice scores (larger is better), which is a similarity coefficient commonly used to assess image segmentation quality. The test set average Dice score is 0.865 and relative L^1(D) error is 0.264. We also compute an average ``L^0(D) norm'' error of 0.197, which is the area of the region where the true and predicted conductivities differ. These are excellent scores considering how challenging this discontinuous dataset is.

For t>1, gives the second inequality. The case tleq -1/2 follows from . Finally, the inequality holds for -1/2<tleq 1 by .
